survey: A cartoon toy rocket tilted up and to the right, floating against a blue sunburst background. Parts: (1) A glossy red ogive nose cone that sits on the body, with a rolled red collar ring at the joint. The ring wraps evenly all the way around. (2) A silver cylindrical body that tapers slightly toward the base. (3) Two round portholes stacked along the body's front centerline, each with a bronze bezel and blue glass. Both are seated flush in the hull and foreshortened the same way, which fits the body's curve. (4) Two red swept fins on the left and right of the lower body. Each root edge meets the hull along its length, and both reach a little below the base, as tail fins normally do. The left fin faces the camera more and the right one is turned away, so the size difference comes from perspective, not a mirroring fault. A third fin hidden behind the body is implied, which is a normal simplification. (5) A black nozzle ring at the base. (6) A small yellow-orange exhaust flame coming out of the nozzle centre. The flame is a real working part of a rocket, not an invented one. Floating is expected because the rocket is shown in flight.
